import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 536

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/536](https://www.erdosproblems.com/536)
-/

namespace Erdos536

open Finset Nat Filter

/--
Let $\epsilon>0$ and $N$ be sufficiently large. Is it true that if $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has
size at least $\epsilon N$ then there must be distinct $a,b,c\in A$ such that
$$[a, b]=[b, c]=[a, c],$$
where $[\cdot, \cdot]$ denotes the least common multiple?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_536 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (ε > (0: ℝ)), ∀ᶠ N in atTop,
    ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), A ⊆ Icc 1 N → (ε * (N : ℝ)) ≤ (A.card : ℝ) →
    ∃ᵉ  (a ∈ A) (b ∈ A) (c ∈ A),
    # {a, b, c} = 3 ∧ a.lcm b = b.lcm c ∧ b.lcm c = a.lcm c := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): add the statements from the additional material

end Erdos536

reformulations.difference: The source defines f(N) as the largest size of an LCM-triangle-free subset of {1,…,N} and explicitly asks whether f(N)=o(N). Lean instead asks whether every subset of size at least εN contains an LCM triangle, for every ε>0 and all sufficiently large N. Distinctness is expressed by #{a,b,c}=3.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The family of triangle-free subsets of {1,…,N} is finite and contains the empty set, so its maximum cardinality f(N) is attained. Consequently, every subset of size at least εN contains a triangle exactly when f(N)<εN. Requiring this eventually for every ε>0 is equivalent to f(N)=o(N); in the reverse direction, use the little-o bound with ε/2 and restrict eventually to N>0. Finset.card_triple_eq_three_iff gives precisely pairwise distinctness, and Filter.eventually_atTop yields a threshold depending on ε but uniform over A. These equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/equivalence.lean. The extremal-function equivalence uses only standard foundational axioms, not the sorry-backed conjecture.
